acceptance: Partitioning balances by recorded per-test duration
Worst-shard time within about 15% of the mean across at least 10 PR runs
Medium critical path shorter than the pre-shrink unit chain
Shard coverage evidence still verifies every collected test
context:
Corrected after review: the original item named shard 3 from stale data. Related open item ci-amplab-generate-data-timeout-flake covers the generate_data timeout.

Duration data (checked 2026-10-20): there is no usable per-test duration source today. tests/fixtures/test_durations.json is bootstrap-only with 0 tests, the shard evidence plugin (scripts/pytest_shard_evidence.py) records no durations, and CI logs show only --durations=25. A duration-weighted partition therefore needs a new source first, for example per-shard --junitxml artifacts merged by _project/scripts/update_test_durations.py, plus a greedy longest-first assignment with a fallback for unknown tests. Not implemented. The speed of the slowest shard is also affected by the cold-cache cost tracked in ci-medium-collect-cold-cache-cost.
description: Medium-test shards are assigned round-robin over the sorted node ids (scripts/release_canary_sharding.py partition_node_ids: ordered[shard_index::shard_count]), which balances test count, not time. Measured over the 20 most recent completed PR CI runs with all four shards (2026-10-19 14:09Z to 2026-10-20 12:41Z), shard 0 was the slowest in 20 of 20. Typical times were shard 0 at 640-1040 s against 330-700 s for the others, because a few very slow tests land on shard 0 (tests/test_h2odb.py::TestH2ODB::test_generate_data alone took 353 s on run 39180253922, tests/test_ssb.py generate_data 95 s). An earlier analysis (runs to 2026-10-18 17:02Z) found shard 3 slowest at 841 s; that no longer holds after later changes, so re-measure before choosing a fix. The claim that medium-shard PRs are 3% slower end to end comes from that earlier analysis and is not re-verified here.
